title: Square of Any Size
body:
Goal: the program asks "How big?" and draws a square that size.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run (F5).
  2. Click in the Shell (the bottom part of Thonny), type 120 and press Return. Oh no - a red error! This is the bug hunt.
  3. The clue: input always gives back text, like "120", not the number 120. The turtle cannot walk "120" steps.
  4. Fix it: turn the text into a number with int(...): size = int(answer)
  5. Run it again and try different sizes: 50, 150, 250.

Done looks like: whatever number you type, the turtle draws a square with sides that long.

Extra: ask a second question, "How thick is the pen? (1 to 10)", and use the answer in t.pensize(...).

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the line where the program makes size, and read the BUG HUNT note above it. Then read the red error message in the Shell. It hints that something is the wrong kind of thing.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: When you type in the Shell, input() gives back text, even if you type digits. The turtle needs a real number to walk. Python has a command that changes text into a whole number.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: The command is int( ). Put the name of the thing that holds what you typed inside the parentheses, like int(____). Use it on the line that sets size. Then run it and try a few sizes.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Square of Any Size
# input() asks a question in the Shell and waits for an answer.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")
t.color("#D55E00")
t.pensize(3)

answer = input("How big should the square be? (try 50 to 250) ")

# BUG HUNT: input() always gives back TEXT, like "120".
# TODO: turn the text into a number with int( )
size = answer

print("Drawing a square with sides of", size)

for i in range(4):
    t.forward(size)
    t.left(90)

turtle.done()
